tickets.title: The first answer's content read: a machine holding nothing reaches the published content in one trip (**amendment 13, E27, 2026-10-28**)

authority.locator: E27 · section 2 of amendment 13, "Done when" (P97's root-cause analysis, R-P547; the diagnosis S44/analyst-stamps-content, R-P553; in force under the owner's direction of 28 October, R-P545; section 3 row 1 as amended for E27)
authority.requirement: a publication's set and documents are kept for as long as memory allows (the head still checked on every decision); the head carries each document's version so a machine holding nothing reads the content in one round, existing tenants backfilled without an operator's publication; a brand-new machine reaches the content in one trip; the per-trip storage time reported so the stamps' slower trip is measured live; the answers identical; the stamps' cold first answer within about 300 ms of server time once P97 ships.

tickets.outcome: A decision on a machine holding nothing reaches the tenant's published content in one storage trip, and a machine that read the publication before pays only the head's check at any age, with the same answers and a publication still honoured on the very next read, so the stamps' cold first answer lands within about 300 ms of server time once P97 ships.

criteria.observable: Fix A, on both hosts: a machine that has read a publication's set and documents keeps them, by the identity of that set (its revision and digest) and its backing binding, for as long as memory allows: a later decision that finds the same committed head, at any time after (past 30 s included), reads the head alone. The head is still read and checked on every decision by a new handle (Lane E4), so a publication committed between two decisions is served on the very next one; what is held is bounded in bytes (the least recently used leaving first), cleared by invalidatePublicationCache and by the writers' invalidation, never used by an administrative read, and never answers when the head cannot be read. In the harness at 100 ms a read, an idle machine's documents stage (past 30 s) is one wave of reads, counted from the read log, and at most 150 ms, the midpoint between one wave and two (R-P580 F5) (the design measured 305 ms today, 101–104 ms with A; _evidence/parity-step3/S44/analyst-stamps-content/logs/03-probe-summary.md). Today a serving entry lapses 30 s after the read that made it (PUBLICATION_CACHE_MS, src/config/publication.ts:8; fresh, :455; pinPublication, :482–508), although a set and its documents never change once published, so a decision past 30 s reads the head, the set and the documents again (lane L20: the pair's held page views at 32 s paid 228 and 242 ms).
criteria.proof: The P102 acceptance command runs the tests named unit:P102.CR1 in src/units/P102/LEDGER.unit.test.ts and they pass, and the program integration gate command exits 0 at the same artifact revision.

criteria.observable: Fix B, on both hosts: the commit (finish, src/config/publication.ts:899–910, the head written at :905) writes the revision of each member of the committed set as the head object's storage metadata; the head's JSON, its digest and its field set are unchanged (loadHead's checks, :318–337), so code that does not know the metadata reads the head exactly as before (a rollback to older code is safe). A decision on a machine holding nothing names its members (the content, slots, learn and reflex documents, src/content/service.ts:764–771) and reads the set and those members in one round after the head: two storage trips, not three. A member whose revision, digest or index row differs from the set's own ref is read again from the set as today, so the metadata is a hint and never authority (a hint naming absent revisions, a stale revision or malformed text gives the identical answer). Existing tenants' heads gain the metadata without an operator's publication: a one-time backfill off every shopper's time, from the five-minute scheduled run (src/index.ts:282–329), rewrites a committed head that lacks it with the same bytes under a conditional write on its etag, so a publication committed meanwhile wins and the backfill then changes nothing, and a publication that meets the backfill's rewrite of its head is not refused for it; the synthetic monitor's reads answer as today (src/ops/synthetic.ts:211–223). In the harness at 100 ms a read, with A and B and no serving copy, a machine holding nothing spends two waves of reads in documents, counted from the read log, and at most 250 ms, the midpoint between two waves and three (R-P580 F5) (the design measured 307 ms today, 205–211 ms with B). Today a cold decision reads the head (publication.ts:489, loadHead :318–337), then the set (:497, currentSet :409–412), then the four documents together (service.ts:766–771 through publication.ts:528–545): three sequential trips (_evidence/parity-step3/S44/analyst-stamps-content/DESIGN.md §2, REPRODUCED in the harness and in local workerd).
criteria.proof: The P102 acceptance command runs the tests named unit:P102.CR2 in src/units/P102/LEDGER.unit.test.ts and they pass, and the program integration gate command exits 0 at the same artifact revision.

criteria.observable: Fix C, on both hosts: a brand-new machine, holding nothing of the tenant, reaches the published content in one storage trip. Every commit also writes one serving copy of the committed set and its members' documents under a fixed name per scope, at most 1 MiB (above it no copy is written and a reader takes CR2's two trips); a decision holding nothing reads the head and that copy together, and uses the copy only where its set digest equals the head's committed identity and every member matches its ref in the set, else reads as CR2 (a stale or missing copy costs one parallel read and never changes an answer); existing tenants' copies are written by CR2's backfill. In the harness at 100 ms a read, a machine holding nothing spends at most 150 ms in documents (the midpoint between one wave and two, R-P580 F5), in one wave of reads issued together, counted from the read log (today 307 ms in three waves; A and B 205–211 ms in two; the design's §8 projects one wave, about A's idle 101–104 ms). P93's anchored product page then reads at most 4 objects cold: the head, the serving copy, the anchor's shard and its part. Today the commit writes nothing beside the head, the set and the revisions (finish, src/config/publication.ts:899–910), and a page reads 8 objects cold (P93 CS2).
criteria.proof: The P102 acceptance command runs the tests named unit:P102.CR3 in src/units/P102/LEDGER.unit.test.ts and they pass, and the program integration gate command exits 0 at the same artifact revision.

criteria.observable: Every decision's answer reports the storage trips its documents stage waited on, in whole milliseconds and in order, each by what it read (the head; the set and members, or the serving copy; nothing where it was held), in a body member beside sources.timings that kit 02 names, on the first-request door's answer and on a held session's; Server-Timing and sources.timings are unchanged (P76's five stages and their add-up, P96's one total). The live lane can then split a stamp's time per trip from the number of trips. Today the documents stage is timed only as a whole (src/content/service.ts:757–760, the lap at :795), so the stamps' 275 ms median against the pair's 161 ms was split into trips only by fitting (_evidence/parity-step3/S44/analyst-stamps-content/DESIGN.md §1, §3: about 92 ms a trip on the stamps against 54 ms on the pair, HYPOTHESIS).
criteria.proof: The P102 acceptance command runs the tests named unit:P102.CR4 in src/units/P102/LEDGER.unit.test.ts and they pass, and the program integration gate command exits 0 at the same artifact revision.

criteria.observable: LOCK, on both hosts, with A, B and C on: the answers identical to today's (the versions, the decisions, the experiment, the context key) on a cold, an idle and a warm machine and across a publication committed between two decisions; one pinned set per decision, every document validated against it; P93's page (unit:P93.CS2: at most 8 reads cold, the same classes, warm no shard or part, its read list as re-pointed by this ticket's R10 to C's reads); src/config/versionedStore.test.ts (W11.02, in workerd on native R2), src/config/publication.optionalMember.test.ts and src/config/publication.servingCache.test.ts (as re-pointed by the R10); and the 26 lock files the design ran green under A and B, 493 tests (_evidence/parity-step3/S44/analyst-stamps-content/logs/05-locks-AB.log): P13, P76, P84, P30, P96, P86, P80, P81, P85, P36, P60, LANDING, W16 C2, C2b, C3, C4 and C6, W18 B1, W19 B1, B2 and B3, W37 FIX2, FIX3, LEDGER and T7, and P95.
criteria.proof: The P102 acceptance command runs the tests named unit:P102.CR5 in src/units/P102/LEDGER.unit.test.ts and they pass, and the program integration gate command exits 0 at the same artifact revision.

criteria.observable: Lane L21 on the pair and on the stamps (staging and production, the stamps read-only), at the release that carries this ticket and P97: the stamps' cold first answer within about 300 ms of server time (the door's total; projected today 174–502 ms, _evidence/parity-step3/S44/analyst-stamps-content/DESIGN.md §7); the per-trip split recorded from CR4 on both pair hosts and both stamps (how many trips each documents stage made and what each cost), so why a stamp's storage trip costs about 1.7 times the pair's (92 ms against 54 ms, R-P553) is measured live; the stamps' pilot tenant read with its head's member metadata and serving copy present without any operator's publication (the backfill).
